checks.detail: TESS Input Catalog v8.2; luminosity class dwarf

checks.name: Companion radius
checks.detail: Jupiter-sized: brown dwarfs and low-mass stars have this radius too, so only a mass (RVs) can tell

checks.name: Host type
checks.detail: a main-sequence dwarf (Teff 4245 K)

checks.name: Multiplicity
checks.detail: no sign of a companion in Gaia DR3 (astrometry, image shape, orbit and binary tables) or on ExoFOP
checks.value: Gaia DR3 RUWE 0.96, IPD harmonic 0.033, multi-peak 1% · ExoFOP companions 0

checks.name: Already catalogued
checks.detail: not a TOI, CTOI, known planet or catalogued binary at this period
checks.value: checked: TOIs, CTOIs, confirmed planets, TESS EB catalog, AAVSO VSX, Gaia DR3 eclipsing binaries and orbits

checks.name: Period recovery
checks.detail: found the 31 ppt transit 1 more time in TESS (BTJD 1389.59; same depth and duration, above the 7.0σ false-alarm threshold); the dips don't fit one period without predicting a transit where TESS saw none: not one transiting body, or the repeats are something else; most probable P ≈ 268 d (68%: 168-473 d), from the periods the data allow, the transit probability and the shape's 104 d; a second transit fixes it: the next TESS sectors of the star, or ground photometry
checks.value: 16 sectors scanned (344 d): BTJD 1389.59, 22.1 ppt, SNR 65.9 · ZTF has too few points on the star · 34% of 58.2-2000 d allowed by the TESS coverage

checks.name: Individual transits
checks.detail: one transit: the period is unknown
checks.value: BTJD 1391.13: vetting SNR 60.4, 33.6 ppt (the search's SNR was 111: a different detrending, binning and noise estimate)

checks.name: Event consistency
checks.detail: compares transits with each other: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Signal uniqueness (single event)
checks.detail: a brightening at BTJD 1393.73 is also above the false-alarm threshold: the systematics make events this size in both directions
checks.value: the dip 70.0σ white, 67.2σ red (F_red 1.04 from 1210 box positions over 343 d); threshold 4.3σ (noise reaches it anywhere in that much data 1% of the time); strongest brightening 82.3σ red at BTJD 1393.73

checks.name: SNR growth
checks.detail: how the SNR builds over transits: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Period consistency
checks.detail: one transit: there's no period to check (the alias and shape checks bound it instead)

checks.name: Alias periods
checks.detail: periods under 6.9 d would have shown a second transit in the data around the dip; on this star a 6.80 h transit needs P ≳ 77.1 d (central, circular orbit)

checks.name: Detrending sensitivity
checks.detail: survives 4 detrendings (two methods, transits masked) with the depth within 30%
checks.value: running median 0.83 d: 34 ppt (SNR 62.6); running median 1.33 d: 33.6 ppt (SNR 63.0); running median 2.33 d: 33.8 ppt (SNR 71.8); local quadratic 1.67 d: 33.5 ppt (SNR 63.8)

checks.name: Depth stability
checks.detail: one transit: nothing to compare its depth with (the pipeline and detrending checks test it instead)

checks.name: Odd/even depths
checks.detail: one transit: there are no alternate transits to compare

checks.name: Secondary eclipse
checks.detail: a deeper eclipse at BTJD 1394.01 (309 ppt, 9.2× this dip): the star eclipses, and this dip is most likely its secondary eclipse
checks.value: deepest other dip: BTJD 1394.01, 309 ppt (92.7σ red); limit for an eclipse anywhere in 343 d of data: 0.91 ppt (3σ red)

checks.name: Transit shape
checks.detail: asymmetric: the first half is 28% deeper (21.1σ)
checks.value: T14 6.80 h, ingress 1.70 h (50% of the half-duration); depth 46.5 ppt

checks.name: Duration vs expected
checks.detail: with no period, the duration bounds it instead: P ≳ 77.1 d on this star (central, circular orbit)

checks.name: Period from the transit shape
checks.detail: the transit's shape on this star implies P ≈ 104 d, consistent with the data showing no other transit
checks.value: P ≈ 104 d (range ~51.8-207 d for modest eccentricity) from T14 6.80 h, ingress 1.70 h and ρ★ 2.43 ρ☉; the data allow P > 77.1 d

checks.name: Variability at the transit period
checks.detail: no variability above 0.5 ppt out of transit (smaller pulsations are handled by the pulsation test)

checks.name: Pulsation removal
checks.detail: the transit survives subtracting the star's pulsations, at the same depth
checks.value: 1 periodic signal removed: 25.8 h (0.3 ppt); transit 33.6 ppt (SNR 60.4) → 33.6 ppt (SNR 60.4), 8 sectors

checks.name: Archival radial velocities
checks.detail: Gaia sees the star's radial velocity vary (χ² p ≤ 0.01, renormalised GoF > 4) by as much as a stellar companion would: a spectroscopic binary
checks.value: Gaia: 36 epochs, p(constant) 0.0000017, robust amplitude 27.2 km/s → K < 26.3 km/s · APOGEE: RV scatter 0.0523 km/s

checks.name: Centroid shift
checks.detail: no significant centroid motion: the source is within ~11″ of the target (3σ)

checks.name: Difference imaging
checks.detail: ran on 1 sector, but no source visible in the pixels (2.7σ): the transit is too shallow for TESS's full-frame images; it can't say which star dims

checks.name: Aperture dependence
checks.detail: large/small depth ratio 2.88 (44.5σ). Not scored: QLP's 1x1 and 5x5 px apertures aren't dilution-corrected, and known on-target planets differ by up to 3x too; a pixel-level (TPF) test is needed

checks.name: Nearby sources
checks.detail: 2 stars within 1′ (3 TESS pixels) could make the dip and the pixel and centroid tests rule out the other 6: needs seeing-limited photometry of the neighbours on a transit night
checks.value: 8 of 103 Gaia DR3 stars within 2′ could cause a 33.6 ppt dip if eclipsed: Gaia 5281640722640603264 at 2″, T 12.3 (needs a 7% eclipse); Gaia 5281640722640603136 at 7″, T 14.6 (needs a 31% eclipse); Gaia 5281640550841912192 at 51″, T 14.6 (needs a 32% eclipse); Gaia 5281640482122455168 at 74″, T 15.2 (needs a 55% eclipse)

checks.name: Unresolved companions
checks.detail: Gaia sees no companion beyond ~1″ (131 au at 131 pc), and RUWE 0.96 disfavours bright ones at ~0.1-1″; closer than ~0.5-1″ (66 au at 131 pc) only speckle/AO imaging can look (the statistical validation below allows for them)

checks.name: Ground photometry (ZTF archive)
checks.detail: folds ZTF on an ephemeris: none yet without a period

checks.name: Saturation
checks.detail: too faint to saturate

checks.name: Crowding
checks.detail: 11% of the light is from other stars

checks.name: Independent pipelines
checks.detail: no sector with a transit has a second pipeline's light curve

checks.name: Another season
checks.detail: a single transit can only be in one season

checks.name: False-positive probability
checks.detail: a nearby star is the most likely source (an approximate TRICERATOPS-style calculation, assuming P ≈ 268 d (the most probable period) as TRICERATOPS does for single transits: run TRICERATOPS with a contrast curve before claiming validation)
checks.value: FPP 71%, NFPP 57%; most likely: Planet transits neighbour Gaia 5281640722640603136 27%, Planet transits the target 22%, Planet transits neighbour Gaia 5281640722640603264 21%

checks.name: Follow-up observations
checks.detail: not recommended: rejected above
